newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end down, spots up.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end down, spots up.

text.p: Contracts on the treasury bill repurchase market in Shanghai closed mostly down on Friday mainly because of reduced trading by big institutions ahead of the weekend when there was no new A share issue, traders said.
The annual rate for the most actively traded seven-day contract fell to 7.00 percent from 12.00 percent on Thursday.
Total turnover of the six-contract market fell to 1.4 million losts from 3.1 million lots.
One lot is 1,000 yuan face value of treasury bills.
"Big institutions cut their trading today due to a lack of new A share issues on Thursday and Friday," one trader said. "That pushed both the repo rates and volume down."
Traders said they expected the rates to experience a slight technical rebound early next week.
Contracts on the T-bill spot market in Shanghai ended up across the board on Friday on a technical rebound supported by the contracts' high yields, traders said.
The most actively traded 10-year bond that matures in June 2006 rose to 109.45 yuan from 108.58 yuan.
Combined volume of the eight-contract market fell to 924,741 lots from 1.2 million lots.
The contracts had been on a downward trend in the past few weeks, partly due to the active stock markets attracting liquidity from the spot market despite the current high yields.
Traders said they believed prices would continue to rise slowly early next week.
